audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 2, 3 and 4 were given to Skill/Swain/Swain while the whys on the very same rows argue Ziggs wins them.
audit.why: whys[1] says his slow W and dodgeable E cannot answer your bomb; whys[2] says you zone with the minefield and keep chunking; whys[3] says your artillery poke dominates before his R comes online. The mirror set rows 1-6 to the packet chart (Ziggs x5, then Swain), which matches those whys. I left row 7 as Swain because whys[6], spikes[3] and late all concede the late game to a drain-tank Swain.
audit.corrected: Ziggs / Ziggs / Ziggs / Ziggs / Ziggs / Swain / Swain — matched full/content pairs with ratings.

audit.why: The spike order is right and already numbered where it matters: Swain's real spike is first item plus Demonic Ascension (flat 120s), and that is where the chart flips. Mega Inferno Bomb at 6 (5000 range, 120/95/70) does not change who wins the lane, and spikes[1] already says so.
sources: kits: swain R cd 120 range 650; ziggs R 5000 cd 120/95/70

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is described only as 'a dodgeable skillshot root'. Riot's text says the wave goes out, RETURNS, and roots on the way back — and Swain can then pull rooted champions toward him. The page also never states how short Demonic Ascension actually is.
audit.why: Nevermove: 850 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, roots on the return and enables a pull, with a shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension. Demonic Ascension is only 650 range on a flat 120s — it is a drain, not a gap-closer, so the root is the entire combo. Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently raises his max health off Soul Fragments, which is why anti-heal timing matters and why raw resistances are the wrong answer.
audit.corrected: Nevermove roots on the RETURN, not the outbound pass, and he can pull rooted targets in — step through the first wave and be moving when it comes back. Demonic Ascension only reaches 650, so with the root dodged it feeds on minions instead of you.
sources: kits: swain E text/range 850/cd 12-10, R range 650 cd 120, P Ravenous Flock text

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracked Demonic Ascension, which is the wrong clock.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is indefinite while he keeps draining, so it is not a window you count down. Nevermove at 12s and 850 range is the cooldown that decides whether stepping up is safe.
sources: kits: swain E cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, R 'indefinite as long as Swain drains'

edits.after: Nevermove roots on the RETURN, not the way out — the wave passes you once, then comes back, and he can drag rooted targets in. Step through the outbound wave and be moving when it returns; it is 850 range on 12 seconds.

notes: Best find: Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass and lets Swain pull rooted champions in — the page called it 'a dodgeable skillshot root', which teaches the wrong dodge. Paired with it: Demonic Ascension is only 650 range on a flat 120s and is indefinite while draining, so it is not a cooldown you count and it cannot close a gap on its own; the whole matchup is the root. Chart rows 2-4 flipped to Ziggs to match both the packet chart and their own whys, which already argued Ziggs wins those stages. I left the 2+ items row with Swain: whys[6], spikes[3] and late all concede the late game to a drain-tank, and the mirror only specified rows 1-6. The packet suspectName 'Your Mega Inferno Bomb' is a false positive — correct name with a possessive. Anti-heal is already prescribed in report[8], and I reinforced the reason in wants.foe[1].
